collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HISTORY AND COLLECTIVE MEMORY (HIS-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Old stories, ruins and abandoned places, heirlooms, disputed records, festivals that changed, names on carvings, customs nobody can explain, and the things a people remembers together: some of it painful and handled gently, some of it gloriously silly.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a child aged 5-12)

collection.description: On the yearly quiet day, a small child whispers how much longer: explain it simply, or go for a quiet walk.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Once a year, there's a quiet day. No drums, no games, no shouting. Long ago, so the story goes, a sickness swept through the island, and many people died, and those who lived made a promise to remember them with a day of quiet. (friend) has been asked to play silently, and has been sitting very still for about as long as a small child possibly can. (friend.He/she) whispers to (subject): "How much longer?"

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) whispers back: "Today we're remembering people who got sick a long time ago. Being quiet is how we do it." (friend) thinks. "Can I remember them while I play with the crab?" (subject) thinks too. "Quietly?" (friend) nods. "Then yes." (friend) plays with the crab very, very quietly, which is probably what the old people would have wanted.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) takes (friend) for a quiet walk along the beach, where (friend.he/she) can move without disturbing anyone. They don't talk. They pick up shells. They watch the waves. When they come back, (friend) asks, in a whisper, why the sick people died. (subject) says nobody knew how to help them, back then. (friend) holds (subject.his/her) hand the rest of the way.
